explanation: Article 4 makes admission a decision of the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council, which means a permanent member can hold an applicant out indefinitely — and from 1946 both blocs did exactly that, so that membership became a currency rather than a status. Portugal, refused for nine years, entered in December 1955 in a package of sixteen states agreed between the blocs to clear the backlog. The design of the Charter is why the admission took the form of a bargain over a list rather than a judgement on Portugal, and it is also why what Portugal found inside was an Assembly majority it could not veto.
